Area of polygons: Area measures the surface inside a figure in square units. Rectangle: length x width. Parallelogram: base x height. Triangle: one half x base x height. Trapezoid: one half x (b1 + b2) x height. Rhombus or kite: one half x d1 x d2. Regular polygon: one half x apothem x perimeter. Irregular shapes can be split into simpler shapes whose areas are added or subtracted.
Prisms and cylinders: A prism has two parallel congruent bases joined by rectangles, and a cylinder has two parallel circular bases. Volume of both is base area x height (V = B x h). Lateral surface area is the perimeter of the base times the height, and total surface area is the lateral area plus two bases. For a cylinder, V = pi r^2 h and total surface area = 2 pi r h + 2 pi r^2. Cavalieri's principle says solids with equal heights and equal cross-section areas have equal volumes.
Pyramids, cones and spheres: A pyramid or cone has volume one third of the matching prism or cylinder: V = (1/3) B h for a pyramid and V = (1/3) pi r^2 h for a cone. Surface area uses the slant height: for a regular pyramid L = (1/2) x perimeter x slant height, and for a cone L = pi r l. A sphere has volume (4/3) pi r^3 and surface area 4 pi r^2. The slant height, height and radius (or apothem) form a right triangle.
Cross sections of solids: A cross section is the shape you get when a plane slices through a solid. A plane parallel to the base of a prism or cylinder gives a shape congruent to the base, and for a pyramid or cone gives a shape similar to the base. A plane through the axis of a cylinder gives a rectangle, and any plane through a sphere gives a circle. Solids can also be made by rotating a plane figure around a line (solids of revolution).
